_comment: What a clean install actually contains, measured rather than assumed.
This file exists so that a missing texture is not mistaken for a broken install. Somebody
setting SCOPE up for the first time, human or agent, opens a scene, sees that 46 images
cannot be found, and reasonably concludes the download failed. It did not. Those files were
never published because they were never recoverable: the scene authors used relative paths
pointing outside the scene folder, and in two cases an absolute path into a paid Blender
addon on the original author's own machine.
scripts/06_verify_setup.py checks against this and reports three outcomes rather than one:
matches expected  the install is correct, even where files are absent
worse             more is missing than should be, so the download or unpack failed
better            fewer are missing, so a scene has been fixed and this file is stale
None of it affects a benchmark run. Captures use studio lighting with the scene world off,
so a missing sky never reaches the model, and the absent surface textures in postwar-city
show as one magenta door and a few flat panels in a scene that is otherwise complete.

book-nook.note: Complete. The only scene with a working sky, an 8K HDRI packed into the .blend. Captures do not draw it, because they use studio lighting with the scene world off, so it makes no difference to a run.

city-street.note: Complete. It has no world environment texture at all, which is how it was authored rather than something absent. This scene is far more expensive to shade under software OpenGL than the other three, and the cost does not fall with resolution; see docs/SETUP.md.

postwar-city.note: 46 surface textures are absent and not recoverable from any published source. They live under texture/batiment, texture/ciment, texture/route, texture/barriere, texture/plantes and world/masks, by relative paths pointing outside the scene folder. The scene renders usably without them: one magenta door and a few flat panels. Two further images are generated procedurally, so they are neither packed nor missing.

whitechapel.note: Five absent. Two are HDRIs from a paid Blender addon on the original author's machine, one is from a stock site that no longer exists, two are scene-author textures. The sky has never worked in this scene; that is its original state rather than a regression, and studio lighting means it is never drawn.
